AlberdiLab | Aizpurua et al. 2025 Ancestral traits of Greenland’s Qimmit sled dog gut microbiomes Ostaizka Aizpurua1 Antton Alberdi2 Last update: 2026-04-22 Chapter 1 Introduction This webbook contains all the code used for data analysis in study of gut microbiomes of newts across ponds included in a restoration plan. 1.1 Prepare the R environment 1.1.1 Environment To reproduce all the analyses locally, clone this repository in your computer using: RStudio > New Project > Version Control > Git And indicating the following git repository: https://github.com/alberdilab/sled_dogs_extended.git Once the R project has been created, follow the instructions and code chunks shown in this webbook. 1.1.2 Libraries The following R packages are required for the data analysis. # Base library(R.utils) library(knitr) library(tidyverse) library(devtools) library(tinytable) library(rairtable) library(janitor) library(broom) # For tree handling library(ape) library(phyloseq) library(phytools) # For plotting library(ggplot2) library(ggrepel) library(ggpubr) library(ggnewscale) library(gridExtra) library(ggtreeExtra) library(ggtree) library(ggh4x) library(UpSetR) library(viridis) # For statistics library(spaa) library(vegan) library(Rtsne) library(geiger) library(hilldiv2) library(distillR) library(ANCOMBC) library(lme4) library(nlme) library(pairwiseAdonis) library(emmeans) library(pheatmap) library(rstatix) library(broom) University of Copenhagen, ostaizka.aizpurua@sund.ku.dk↩︎ University of Copenhagen, antton.alberdi@sund.ku.dk↩︎

Chapter 2 Prepare data Load the original data files outputted by the bioinformatic pipeline. 2.0.1 Reads read_counts <- read_tsv("data/counts.tsv") %>% rename(genome=1) %>% rename_with(~ str_remove(.x, "_EKDL.*")) %>% rename_with(~ str_remove(.x, "_M$")) 2.0.2 Sample metadata sample_metadata <- read_csv("data/sample_metadata.csv") %>% left_join(sample_metadata_illu[c(1,4,9)], by=join_by("sample"=="DogID")) %>% filter(!Samples %in% c("Blank", "Saliva")) %>% select(sample, breed, origin, country, locality) metadata_new1 <- read_csv("data/PRJEB85799.csv") %>% rename(country=notes) %>% rename(sample=name) sample_metadata <- read_csv("data/meta_new.csv") %>% select(-"Research agreement",-"Owner age range") %>% rename(breed=Breed) %>% rename(origin="Origin of the dog") %>% rename(locality=District) %>% rename(sample=Code)%>% left_join(., metadata_new1[c(3,4)], by="sample")%>% select(sample, breed, origin, country, locality) %>% bind_rows(sample_metadata) 2.0.3 Filter read counts read_counts <- read_counts %>% select(one_of(c("genome",sample_metadata$sample))) %>% filter(rowSums(. != 0, na.rm = TRUE) > 0) %>% select_if(~!all(. == 0)) 2.0.4 Genome taxonomy genome_taxonomy <- read_tsv("data/genome_taxonomy.tsv") %>% rename(genome = user_genome) %>% separate( classification, into = c("domain", "phylum", "class", "order", "family", "genus","species"), sep = ";", # split on the semicolons fill = "right", # if a rank is missing, keep NA on the right remove = TRUE ) %>% mutate(across(domain:species, ~ str_remove(., "^[a-z]__"))) %>% select(genome,domain,phylum,class,order,family,genus,species) %>% filter(genome %in% read_counts$genome) genome_features <- read_tsv("data/quality_report.tsv") %>% rename(genome=1) %>% rename(length=Genome_Size) %>% filter(genome %in% read_counts$genome) genome_metadata <- inner_join(genome_taxonomy,genome_features, by="genome") 2.0.5 Genome base hits genome_coverage <- read_tsv("data/bases.tsv") %>% rename(genome = 1) %>% rename_with( ~ str_remove(.x, "_EKDL.*")) %>% rename_with( ~ str_remove(.x, "_M$")) %>% filter(genome %in% read_counts$genome) %>% select(one_of(c("genome",sample_metadata$sample))) 2.0.6 Genome tree genome_tree <- read_tree("data/gtdbtk.backbone.bac120.classify.tree") genome_tree$tip.label <- str_replace_all(genome_tree$tip.label,"'", "") genome_tree <- keep.tip(genome_tree, tip=genome_metadata$genome) 2.0.7 Genome annotations genome_annotations <- read_tsv("data/gene_annotations.tsv.xz") %>% mutate(genome = str_extract(gene, "^[^^]+")) %>% mutate(ec = str_c("[EC:",ec,"]")) %>% select(genome, everything()) 2.1 Create working objects Transform the original data files into working objects for downstream analyses. 2.1.1 Filter reads by coverage # Keep only genomes and samples present in both datasets common_genomes <- intersect(read_counts$genome, genome_coverage$genome) common_samples <- intersect(colnames(read_counts)[-1], colnames(genome_coverage)[-1]) read_counts <- read_counts %>% filter(genome %in% common_genomes) %>% select(genome, all_of(common_samples)) %>% arrange(match(genome, common_genomes)) genome_coverage <- genome_coverage %>% filter(genome %in% common_genomes) %>% select(genome, all_of(common_samples)) %>% arrange(match(genome, common_genomes)) min_coverage=0.3 # read_counts_filt <- genome_coverage %>% # mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ ifelse(. > min_coverage, 1, 0))) %>% # mutate(across(-1, ~ . * read_counts[[cur_column()]])) read_counts_filt <- read_counts %>% # keep genome column separate select(genome) %>% bind_cols( genome_coverage %>% select(-genome) %>% # drop genome column mutate(across(everything(), ~ as.numeric(. > min_coverage))) %>% # 0/1 coverage map2_df(.x = ., .y = read_counts %>% select(-genome), ~ .x * .y) # multiply by read counts ) 2.1.2 Transform reads into genome counts readlength=150 genome_counts_filt <- read_counts_filt %>% slice(match(genome_metadata$genome, genome)) %>% # reorder rows to match genome_metadata mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ . / (genome_metadata$length / readlength))) 2.1.3 Distill annotations into GIFTs genome_gifts <- distill(genome_annotations,GIFT_db,genomecol=1,annotcol=c(6,8,9), verbosity=TRUE) genome_gifts <- genome_gifts[, !grepl("^S", colnames(genome_gifts))] 2.2 Prepare color scheme AlberdiLab projects use unified color schemes developed for the Earth Hologenome Initiative, to facilitate figure interpretation. phylum_colors <- read_tsv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/earthhologenome/EHI_taxonomy_colour/main/ehi_phylum_colors.tsv") %>% mutate(phylum = str_remove(phylum, "^p__")) %>% right_join(genome_metadata, by=join_by(phylum == phylum)) %>% arrange(match(genome, genome_tree$tip.label)) %>% select(phylum, colors) %>% unique() %>% arrange(phylum) %>% pull(colors, name=phylum) 2.3 Wrap working objects All working objects are wrapped into a single Rdata object to facilitate downstream usage. save(sample_metadata, genome_metadata, # read_counts, # genome_counts, genome_counts_filt, genome_tree, # genome_gifts, phylum_colors, file = "data/data.Rdata") save(genome_gifts, file = "data/genome_gifts1.Rdata")
